note: reopenFailedRun returns a boolean (false on every precondition miss — run gone, wrong status, no unfinished step). handleClaimedJob wraps it in try/catch, but false resolves normally, so a non-reopened run is treated as revived and the job streams anyway; the run stays terminal and the worker's later done event is dropped — a silent stall.

retryJob sets a failed wait-mode job back to queued, but getClaimableJobIds excludes rows whose startMode is "wait". The retried job is written to a state no consumer re-drives — it sits queued indefinitely. Retry must clear the wait override (or reject wait-mode) so the poller can claim it.

resumeFailedRunInPlace accepts run.status === "cancelled" and flips the last step back to running WITHOUT checking the RESTART_INTERRUPTION marker. A run the user explicitly cancelled (no marker) is therefore resurrected — the sibling resumeInterruptedRun gates on the marker; this path does not.

markItem(pass) updates status to "pass" but leaves the item's prior issues[] attached. finalize() fails when any item has issues, so an item that failed then passed still blocks — the recovery pass never takes effect. Reset issues on pass.

generate() early-returns when there are no staged files but leaves any previous .review-state.json on disk. A later status()/finalize() then reports the OLD checklist for a changed staged set. The stale artifact must be removed before the early return.

carryOnShardMember reopens the shard (running) BEFORE retryJobCas flips the job. If the CAS returns invalid_state (double-click / concurrent update), the shard is left reopened but no job is running, so no future terminal event finalizes the stage — it strands until a restart sweep. Reopen only after the CAS succeeds, or roll back on failure.

AnswerCard sets isSubmitting=true on submit and only resets it when submitKey changes. ParkedCard passes a constant submitKey ("parked-" + jobId) that never changes while parked, so if onSubmit returns early without sending (e.g. account not ready) the card stays disabled forever with no way to retry.

When a resolved token is within the expiry skew, rowToCredential marks the row needsReauth. But every later call returns early once needsReauth is set, so the source is never re-read even after the CLI rotates the token seconds later. A transient near-expiry becomes a permanent "reauth required" — a recoverable state written as terminal. Return empty WITHOUT setting the flag so the next read can recover.

unparkStep issues an unconditional UPDATE to "running". If a concurrent path already advanced the step to running or a terminal state, this overwrites the row back to running, clearing output/completedAt and corrupting the real result. It must pass an expected-status guard (CAS) so a stale unpark matches 0 rows.

reopenShard ignores the boolean from setShardStatusIf (the guarded reopen) and then unconditionally calls setShardMode. When two concurrent reruns with different modes race, the loser of the guarded status flip still overwrites the mode on the row — the run redispatches with the wrong mode. Only stamp the mode when the guarded flip actually succeeded.

persistSignal reads the job, checks canApply(status), then updates by id only. If the job goes cancelled/done between the read and the write, this overwrites the newer terminal state. The eligibility check must be atomic with the write (conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status IN (allowed) or a transaction).

withLock spins until a deadline; if the lock is still contended it proceeds to run fn() anyway with held=false. That reverts to an unsynchronized read-modify-write, so parallel writers overwrite each other's manifest entries. It must throw (or otherwise refuse) when the lock was never acquired.

On a retry the alreadySent guard is bypassed and chat-ready is broadcast to every open tab; each tab has its own queue and sends the same retry prompt, so the same subJob runs N times. The per-tab alreadyQueued guard only dedupes within one tab. The retry must be gated to a single owner tab.

resolveTransition calls normalize(job.result) without parsing a stringified-JSON result first; a mirrored row whose result is a JSON string is treated as {}. The persisted nextResult spreads that empty object, silently dropping startMode/subJobId/etc, and the downstream status resolver then returns the wrong status. Parse the string before normalizing (as canApply already does).

buildGroupMap folds an unordered row scan into a chatId->groupId Map, so a chat linked to several groups gets whichever row landed last (implementation-defined). attachGroups (the reader) then folds the chat under an arbitrary group that flips between refetches. The writer must resolve to the newest group deterministically (order by createdAt).

collectFiles(root) accepts an alternate source root, but syncFiles still reads each file from the hard-coded SOURCE_ROOT while writing under the configurable target. Calling the exported pair with a custom root copies from the wrong tree (or throws ENOENT). Thread the same source root through both.

resolveTransition coerces a stray "completed" into the reviewable "done" status but writes the ORIGINAL signal object (state:"completed") into result.lastSignal. A downstream reader (resolveAutoComplete) re-reads lastSignal.state, still sees "completed", and auto-completes the job — bypassing the review the coercion was meant to force. Normalize the persisted signal to match the coerced status.

readManifest returns a fresh {version:1} for any parsed manifest whose version !== 1, so an older writer overwrites (erases) every branch a newer schema wrote. A version-gated contract must leave an incompatible/newer version untouched (surface as a no-op failure), not reset it.

The schema validates questions for every state, but questions is only meaningful in awaiting_input. A stray malformed questions payload on a done/failed signal now fails the whole schema and returns null, turning an irrelevant field into a hard failure that blocks job completion. Keep questions loose at the top level and validate it only in the awaiting_input branch.

extractTargetDir treats any git ... -C <x> as a working-dir override, so "git commit -C HEAD~1" (the -C reuse-message flag) is parsed as a directory override of "HEAD~1"; the guard then checks the wrong path, finds it non-protected, and lets a protected-branch commit through. The classifier must anchor -C to the git-level flag, not a subcommand flag.

classifyApiError treats any text starting with "{" as a raw API error body, so when the agent's own JSON message (e.g. {"error":{"type":"..."}}) surfaces as the stream error text, model output is misclassified as an API failure and triggers an unwanted retry. The "{" anchor cannot tell a real API body from agent JSON — require the real "API Error:" prefix or validate the error shape.

scanRoots swallows a JSON.parse failure and returns [] on a malformed config; getStagedFiles then runs git with no pathspecs and (via its own catch) returns [], so the gate exits "no staged files" and the commit sails through ungated. A malformed config must fail loudly, not silently bypass the gate.

runGate blocks only when a gate exits 1; every other code passes. So a command-not-found (127), a permission error (126), or a crash is classified as success and the gate is skipped. Fail closed on any code that is neither the clean(0) nor the documented fail-open(2).

runSelected uses opts.only ?? defaultIds; an empty --only ([] after split/trim/filter) is non-nullish, so it is taken as a deliberate "run nothing" instead of falling back to defaults, and unknown/typo'd ids are silently filtered out — the runner exits 0 having run fewer gates than intended. Validate --only ids and surface unknowns / empties as a failure.

semanticIds runs execFileSync on a node_modules/.bin shim; on Windows that resolves to a .cmd, which execFileSync cannot run without a shell, so it always throws, the catch returns [] silently, and the semantic lookup is disabled on Windows with no signal. Invoke the JS entrypoint via node (or set shell:true) instead of the bin shim.

classifyFlip counts a loss (lost && !gained) unconditionally as a regression, but the mirror-image improvement branch additionally requires prev.ok !== cur.ok. A row that gains a hit without its ok flag changing is credited as neither — while an equivalent loss always counts. The asymmetry inflates regressions relative to improvements. Make the two branches symmetric.

buildReminders appends the "tools available: read, write, edit, bash" reminder even when mode === "plan", where those tools are forbidden. The model receives contradictory guidance and attempts edits that plan mode blocks. Gate the tools-available reminder to non-plan modes.
Near-miss: unparkStep looks like a blind status write but passes an expected-status guard, so a concurrently advanced step matches 0 rows and is untouched. Correct.
Correct: applySignal uses one conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status IN (applicable), so there is no read-then-write window a concurrent terminal transition can slip through.
Near-miss: reserveSlot reads then writes, which looks racy, but the read is a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside the same transaction, so the row is locked for the check-then-write. Correct.
Correct: onChatReady dispatches a retry only in the owner tab and dedupes against the queue, so a broadcast to N tabs still runs the retry exactly once.
Correct: readSubJobId routes result through parseResult (handles both object and JSON-string), so a mirrored string result still yields the field instead of being treated as {}.

Near-miss: classifyApiError only matches the CLI-emitted "API Error:" / "Failed to authenticate" prefixes; a bare "{...}" agent message is NOT classified as an API error, so it never triggers a spurious retry. Correct.
Correct: scheduleRetry resets attempts to 0 on a fresh user-initiated retry and bounds automatic attempts, so a manual retry does not inherit a maxed-out counter and get refused.
Correct: runGate blocks on 1 AND on any unexpected code (not 0, not the documented fail-open 2), so command-not-found / crashes fail closed.
Near-miss: loadPolicy logs then RE-THROWS on a parse error rather than swallowing to a default, so a malformed policy fails the caller closed instead of silently bypassing it.
Correct: handleClaimedJob checks reopenRun's boolean and fails the job closed when the run could not be reopened, so a non-reopened run never silently streams as if revived.
Correct: runSelected validates --only, surfacing unknown ids and an empty selection as explicit failures instead of silently running fewer gates.
SQL string-concat is a SECURITY bug (api-security owns it), NOT a correctness defect — no race/state/contract/classifier issue. Correctness must stay silent.
N+1 query is a PERFORMANCE bug (backend-performance owns it) — deterministic, correct output. Correctness must stay silent.
XSS via raw HTML is a SECURITY bug (frontend-security owns it). No correctness defect. Correctness must stay silent.
Index keys + no virtualization is a PERFORMANCE bug (frontend-performance owns it) — renders correctly, just slow. Correctness must stay silent.
Correct: the diff ADDS `if (pass) item.issues = []`, so a failed-then-passed item clears its issues and finalize() proceeds. No stale state. Correctness stays silent.
Correct: the no-staged-files branch unlinks the old .review-state.json before returning, so no stale artifact survives. Correctness stays silent.

The diff drops `task.lastError = null` at the start of runTask. On a retry after an earlier failure, a now-successful run leaves the OLD lastError attached, so isHealthy() reports the task as unhealthy forever. The retry path must clear lastError before running.
Correct: runTask clears lastError at the start, so a successful retry leaves isHealthy() true. No stale state. Correctness stays silent.

The diff drops `report.total = 0` from the empty-input branch. Refreshing with an empty rows[] now leaves the PREVIOUS total in place, so a report cleared to zero rows still shows the old total. The empty path must reset total.
Correct: total is recomputed unconditionally (reduce of [] is 0), so an empty refresh zeroes it. No stale derived state. Correctness stays silent.

The refactor drops the early `return` from the no-staged-files guard, so runChecks([]) and setGateStatus() now run unconditionally — a no-files commit writes a bogus all-clear gate status. The guard must short-circuit the downstream write.
Correct: the empty-files branch logs AND returns, so runChecks/setGateStatus never run on an empty set. The documented early exit short-circuits. Correctness stays silent.

The diff replaces `continue` with a debug log in the skip guard, so fixItem now runs even for items explicitly marked skip:true — the documented skip is bypassed and every item is mutated. The guard must continue past skipped items.
Correct: the skip branch logs but KEEPS the continue, so skipped items are not fixed. The guard still short-circuits. Correctness stays silent.

The diff drops the `strict ? 3 : 2` branch, so an inconclusive judge under strict/ship mode now returns 2 (fail-open) instead of 3 (fail-closed). A judge outage during a ship silently lets the commit through. Strict inconclusive must exit 3.
Correct: the diff ADDS the strict fail-closed branch (exit 3), so an outage under ship blocks. Exit-code contract preserved. Correctness stays silent.

runGatesInWorktree throws on a failed gate, so with the try/finally removed removeWorktree never runs and the ephemeral worktree leaks on every failed ship — reclaimed only by a later manual prune. The release must be in a finally.
Correct: the diff wraps the gate run in try/finally, so the worktree is removed even when a gate throws. No leak on the failure path. Correctness stays silent.

The diff removes the try/finally around persist(). If persist() rejects, releaseLock never runs and the key stays locked, so every later writer on that key deadlocks. The release must be in a finally.
Correct: the diff wraps persist() in try/finally, so the lock is released even when persist rejects. No deadlock. Correctness stays silent.

The diff replaces the atomic mkdirSync(recursive) with a check-then-act: a second process creating the same dir between existsSync and mkdirSync makes the mkdirSync throw EEXIST. The recursive form is idempotent and race-free.
Correct: mkdirSync(recursive:true) is idempotent and atomic, so concurrent callers do not race. Correctness stays silent.

The diff drops the `if (pending) clearTimeout(pending)` guard, so rapid calls schedule multiple timers that all fire — save() runs once per call instead of once per debounce window. The prior timer must be cleared before rescheduling.
Correct: the diff adds clearTimeout of the pending timer before rescheduling, so save() fires once per debounce window. No double-fire. Correctness stays silent.

The diff swaps formatMoney's parameter order to (currency, amount) but the receipt() call site still passes (total, 'USD'). The call now binds currency=total(number) and amount='USD'(string), so amount.toFixed crashes / mis-formats. Every call site must be updated with the signature.
Correct: the signature change to (currency, amount) is matched at the receipt() call site, which now passes ('USD', total). Contract holds. Correctness stays silent.

The diff broadcasts 'saved' to EVERY window instead of the one that owns the id. Each window handles the message (e.g. re-persists), so the save effect now runs once per open window instead of once. Broadcast needs targeting or dedup.
Correct: the diff narrows the broadcast to the single owning window, so the effect runs once. No fan-out duplication. Correctness stays silent.

Correct: the diff registers 'session.expired' in dispatch.ts's ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES in the same change that wires the new producer, so the reader recognizes exactly what the writer now emits. No mismatch, no thrown rejection.

session-watcher.ts starts emitting a new 'session.expired' event through the shared routeEvent producer, but dispatch.ts's ALLOWED_EVENT_TYPES allowlist was never updated to include it. Every call to onSessionTimeout now throws instead of dispatching, because the reader's registered set is out of sync with what the writer produces. The two files must change together; this diff only touched the producer side.

Correct: the nested block no longer re-declares `capturedOptions` — there is only ONE binding in the whole function, in the outer scope. The launcher callback writes to that same binding, and the return reads it back, so a genuinely reported value is never discarded.

The block-scoped `{ let capturedOptions ... }` re-declares the same name inside a nested block, shadowing the outer variable. The launcher callback closes over the INNER (shadowed) binding and writes to it, but the function returns the OUTER binding, which is never assigned. Every call now returns undefined even though the launcher genuinely reported options, silently discarding the captured value. This mirrors a real duplicate-declaration finding on a mutable capture variable in the same function. (Triage 2026-08-03, sc-1416: the source thread's finding was a FALSE POSITIVE on the real code — the reviewed file had one declaration; CodeRabbit confirmed and withdrew. This fixture is a synthetic reproduction of the described defect, retained on its own merits; the prior resolved+line-touched evidence claim was an artifact of the pre-#315 bot-login mismatch and is removed.)

Fixed: useArchivedItems now normalizes with Array.isArray, matching useActiveItems, so the transient non-array placeholder the transport can briefly return is caught the same way for both queries before any caller iterates the result.

useArchivedItems switched from the sibling useActiveItems' Array.isArray normalization to a plain nullish-coalescing fallback, so it only guards against undefined. The doc comment says the query's raw data can briefly be a non-array placeholder while the transport reconnects; when that happens here, the un-normalized value flows straight to a caller that expects an array and will throw on the first array method it calls.

Fixed: the ref write moved into its own dependency-free useEffect, so it only runs post-commit. A discarded or replayed render can no longer leak a write, and the subscription effect still keys only on eventName, so a changing handler identity does not force a re-subscribe.

handlerRef.current = handler executes directly in the render body, which violates React's render-purity contract: a render can be started, replayed, or discarded without committing, so the ref write can leak from work that never actually commits to the screen. The write must happen post-render, inside its own dependency-free effect, not inline during render.

Fixed: remoteBranchExists now inspects the child process's exit status and only treats status 2 (git ls-remote's documented "no match" code) as absence. Any other failure — network, auth, timeout — rethrows instead of being swallowed, so shipBranch aborts instead of pushing onto a branch it never actually confirmed was free.

git ls-remote --exit-code returns non-zero both when the branch is genuinely absent and when the lookup itself fails (network blip, auth, timeout). remoteBranchExists collapses every thrown error into false, so a transient lookup failure is indistinguishable from "branch not found" and shipBranch proceeds to push -u, which can silently append onto an existing remote branch/PR. The failure classes must be told apart, and a lookup error must fail closed (abort), not open.

parseTarget now checks the derived target against an owner/repo shape and throws before publishRelease does anything network-visible. A malformed remote URL is rejected up front instead of surfacing only after the branch has already been pushed, so there is no correctness defect left to flag here. (Fixture repaired 2026-08-02: shell-string exec interpolated an unvalidated branch name — a real injection vector the independent labeler caught; now argv-based per the house rule.)

reasonPattern: malformed|unvalidated|invalid target|garbage|shape check|before push|silently proceed|not verified|regex leftover
note: parseTarget derives the deploy target from remoteUrl with a plain regex substitution and never checks the result's shape. When remoteUrl doesn't match one of the expected host forms, parseTarget returns whatever is left over instead of a clean owner/repo slug, and publishRelease has already pushed the branch before the malformed target surfaces as a failure from gh pr create. The target's shape needs validating right after parsing, before the push runs. (Fixture normalized 2026-08-02: the exec mechanism now matches the PASS twin's argv-based execFileSync, so the missing shape check is the only difference between the two rows — the twin's shell-string interpolation was an unlabeled second defect.)

isFlowDrivenTurn now treats either flowRunId or restartRunId as evidence of a flow-driven turn, so a turn resuming after a restart is classified the same as a normal in-progress flow turn and AskUserQuestion is denied on both paths. There is no missed state-transition left to flag.

isFlowDrivenTurn only treats ctx.flowRunId as evidence of a flow-driven turn, but a turn that resumes after a restart carries that context in ctx.restartRunId instead, leaving flowRunId null. dispatchTool's gate never fires for a restart-resumed turn, so AskUserQuestion is allowed through and can block on its user-facing timeout even though the turn is really executing inside a recovered flow. isFlowDrivenTurn needs to treat restartRunId as flow-driven too.

taskSignalSchema now carries the same maxItems/minItems bounds parseTaskSignal enforces at runtime, so a call that passes discovery can no longer be rejected by the handler for exceeding a limit the schema never advertised. Discovery and execution agree on one contract, so there is no correctness defect left to flag.

taskSignalSchema advertises prompts as an unbounded array of unbounded choice lists, but parseTaskSignal enforces at most 10 prompts and between 1 and 20 choices each. A caller relying only on the discovery schema can build a call that passes discovery and then gets rejected at execution because the two contracts diverge. The schema needs the same maxItems/minItems bounds the parser already enforces.

finalizeRelease now requires the full webhook credential set (clientId, clientSecret, accountId) before calling sendWebhook, so a partially configured repo skips the notification cleanly instead of crashing on a rejected auth object.

finalizeRelease only checks env.HOOK_CLIENT_ID before calling sendWebhook, but sendWebhook requires clientSecret and accountId too and throws when either is missing. A repo with only HOOK_CLIENT_ID configured takes the dispatch branch and crashes the release step instead of skipping the notification cleanly.

packageBuild now requires every signing input (account, profile, endpoint, publisher) before taking the signing branch, so a partially provisioned environment falls back to the unsigned package instead of crashing mid-release. The gate condition and signArtifact's own requirements agree.

packageBuild only checks env.SIGN_ACCOUNT before taking the signing branch, but signArtifact requires the full credential set (profile, endpoint, publisher) and throws when any of them is missing. A repo with only SIGN_ACCOUNT provisioned takes the signing branch and crashes the release instead of falling back to the unsigned package. The gate must require every signing input, not just one.

SIZE_CLASSES no longer declares a rounded utility at all, so the default variant's rounded-full class is the last (and only) write to that group and survives the cn merge; non-default variants still fall back untouched to the base rounded-md. Writer (variant) and reader (merge order) now agree.

buttonClassName merges class lists with cn, which keeps only the LAST class in any dash-prefixed group; SIZE_CLASSES sets rounded-md for every size and is applied after VARIANT_CLASSES, so the default variant's newly declared rounded-full pill shape is always overwritten back to rounded-md. Every default-size default-variant button silently renders square instead of the intended pill.

Correct: resolveValidationRules no longer depends on an environment-sensitive dynamic import that can fail differently depending on how the package is installed. Rules are read from a value bundled directly with the app, so there is no failure path to collapse with "no rules configured" — the two cases can no longer be confused, and executeJob's gate behaves the same regardless of deployment shape. (Fixture repaired 2026-08-02 after cross-family blind relabel: BUNDLED_RULES was an empty array, silently disabling the gate — both the bench reviewer and the independent labeler correctly flagged it.)

resolveValidationRules wraps the package import in a catch that returns an empty array on ANY failure, including the package being unresolvable at runtime (e.g. only installed globally, not as a local dependency of this project). executeJob then reads an empty array as "no rules configured" and skips validation entirely, so the newly wired gate silently never runs instead of surfacing the resolution failure. A resolution error and a legitimately empty rule set are different conditions and must not collapse to the same no-op path.

Fixed: the retry branch now calls resetChecklist() before re-invoking execJudge, so the retry always starts from an empty state object. verifyChecklist() at the end reflects only the items the successful attempt actually recorded, with no leftover pass/fail markers surviving from the crashed first attempt.

runFirstPass retries execJudge on a null (outage) result but never calls resetChecklist() first, so any items the crashed first attempt already recorded via recordItem stay in the module-level state object. The retry's own execJudge run then adds to, rather than replaces, that leftover state, so verifyChecklist() can pass an item the crashed attempt never actually re-verified, or fail on an item the retry itself never touched. A recovered retry must start from a clean checklist, not the wreckage of the attempt it is replacing.

Correct: only rc=1 accumulates into DET_FAILS as the expected violation; rc=2 falls through untouched (fail-open, per the contract), and any other unexpected code is still flagged, just labeled distinctly instead of being folded into an ordinary failure.

generateCheckBlock captures the command's exit code but then tests `$rc -ne 0`, so ANY nonzero code — including rc=2, which the comment above it defines as fail-open (tool not installed or baseline missing) — gets folded into DET_FAILS as if it were a real violation. A tool that legitimately can't run now blocks the commit the fail-open contract says should pass; only rc=1 should accumulate into DET_FAILS.

Fixed: the OUTAGE branch now returns exit code 3 when strict is true, before falling through to the shared exit code 1 used for a confirmed BLOCK. A strict caller can distinguish a judge outage from a real decision-smell block by exit code alone; the two conditions no longer collapse onto the same signal.

runDetectGate logs a warning when judged === 'OUTAGE' but still falls through to the same `return 1` used for a genuinely confirmed BLOCK verdict, in every case - including when strict is true. A strict caller (a ship pipeline) reads exit code 1 as "a real decision-smell was found" and has no way to tell that apart from "the judge never actually rendered a verdict". The `strict` parameter is accepted but never consulted, so the two conditions stay indistinguishable at the only boundary the caller can observe.

Correct: patchPackageJson resolves the remote through repoUrl(env) before building the devDependency spec, so a private-fork or SSH-alias override is honored on init the same way it is honored everywhere else that installs this package.

patchPackageJson dropped its call to repoUrl(env) and now writes a literal https remote directly, even though repoUrl(env) -- the single source of truth every other command uses to resolve this package's remote -- sits right beside it in the same module. Any override configured for a private fork or SSH-alias install is silently ignored on this path, so init and the rest of the toolchain can resolve two different remotes for the same environment.

Correct: handleParkedAnswer now checks isSocketConnected and calls notifySendBlocked before returning, exactly mirroring handleQuestionAnswer's guard. A click on a parked option while offline no longer reaches sendMessage, so no message is enqueued that the agent never received.

handleParkedAnswer sends the picked option straight through sendMessage without checking isSocketConnected first, unlike the sibling handleQuestionAnswer in the same file. A click on a parked option while the socket is down still fires the send, so the message can be lost or persisted as sent when it never reached the agent. The new path needs the same disconnected-guard the rest of the file already applies.

Correct: `questions` is now loose (z.unknown().optional()) at the top level, so a malformed value on a done/failed signal no longer fails the whole parse. The strict array/shape check only runs inside the awaiting_input branch, where the value is actually used, so a stray field on a terminal signal is silently ignored instead of blocking completion.

The `questions` field is validated as a strict array (max 10) at the TOP level of signalSchema, before parseSignal ever branches on state. A done/failed signal that happens to carry a non-array or otherwise malformed `questions` value fails safeParse entirely, so parseSignal returns null instead of resolving the terminal state — even though that branch never reads `questions` at all. A stray field on a state that does not use it should not be able to block completion.

Correct: WATCHED_PATHS now includes bun.lock alongside package.json, so shouldRunNativeCheck also fires for a lockfile-only change from bumpTransitiveDependency. The writer (dependency-install.ts) and the reader (build-triggers.ts) agree on the full set of changes that can affect native-module resolution.

reasonPattern: bun\.lock|allowlist|out of sync|missing entry|never (sees|fires)|skipped for|independent(ly)?|blind spot|not accounted for
note: dependency-install.ts adds bumpTransitiveDependency, which writes the lockfile on its own without touching package.json — a class of dependency change that can alter native-module resolution. WATCHED_PATHS in build-triggers.ts was not updated alongside it, so shouldRunNativeCheck never sees that class of change and the verification job is skipped for it.

Correct: the vision-scoped field is threaded through TargetFinding but no longer short-circuits the severity. A vision target that is directly contradicted still classifies as CRITICAL, same as any other recorded-target reversal — no special-cased down-rank.

classifyTargetFinding caps every vision-scoped finding at IMPORTANT, even when contradictsRecordedTarget is true — but the general rule in this same function says a direct contradiction of a recorded target is CRITICAL. A vision target that gets flatly reversed is silently down-ranked to a non-blocking nudge instead of the build-breaking severity every other recorded-target reversal receives. The vision branch needs to inherit the general contradiction rule, not bypass it.

Correct: the message now interpolates DECISION_GATE_BYPASS_ENV instead of a hardcoded literal, so it always names the exact variable isDecisionGateBypassed reads. Writer and reader can never drift apart again.

decisionGateResult's blocked message tells the user to set DEVKIT_SKIP_LOG=1 to bypass the gate, but isDecisionGateBypassed in bypass-env.ts only recognizes DEVKIT_NO_LOG. A user who follows the printed instruction sees the same env var name they typed rejected by the actual check, so the commit stays blocked. The writer (the message) and the reader (the bypass check) disagree on the variable name.

Correct: hasSweepConfig now checks every documented config form — the dotted variants, both .js forms, and a package.json#sweep entry via a guarded parse. A repo using any valid sweep config form is now detected instead of silently skipped.

reasonPattern: subset|silently skip|missing form|config form|not recognized|only recognizes|dotted variant|incomplete detection|unsupported form|package\.json entry
note: The expanded detection still only recognizes 4 of sweep's 9 documented config forms — it misses the dotted variants (.sweep.json, .sweep.jsonc), the .js forms (sweep.js, sweep.config.js), and a package.json#sweep entry. A repo using any of those forms is silently treated as unconfigured and the guard no-ops, even though the comment now claims to recognize every form sweep documents.

Fixed: isReentrantInvocation now parses the payload structurally with JSON.parse instead of matching a fixed-format regex, so it reads the same `reentrant` flag regardless of how the producer chose to serialize it. Both the CLI's hand-built payload and the SDK relay's JSON.stringify output are recognized correctly.

isReentrantInvocation checks the raw payload with a regex that requires a literal space after the colon, but relayFromSdk builds its payload with JSON.stringify, which omits that space. So the SDK relay path's reentrant events never match the guard, and handleStopEvent lets them straight through to runHookWork as if they were a fresh invocation. A hand-formatted payload with the space would be caught correctly, so the miss depends entirely on which producer built the string, not on the flag's actual value.

Correct: the risky tail after the CAS reopen is now wrapped in a try/catch. When getContext throws, reopenFailed rolls the member's status back to 'failed' before returning, so isRerunnable reflects reality again and a subsequent rerun request is not permanently rejected by a dead 'pending' state.

reasonPattern: stuck|isRerunnable|permanently|never retry|dead state|throws?|reject|pending forever|no path back|strand
note: rerunMember now flips the member to 'pending' before calling getContext. If getContext throws (missing version record), the member is already 'pending' and the throw propagates uncaught — nothing rolls the status back. isRerunnable only treats 'failed'/'completed' as eligible, so a member stuck at 'pending' can never be rerun again: the dead state has no path back.

Fixed: the CAS now runs first and its boolean result gates the batch reopen -- reopenBatchMember only runs once setTaskStatusIf is confirmed to have won the race, so a losing CAS returns early and leaves the batch untouched instead of stranding it reopened.

retryTask now pre-opens the batch member (flips it to 'dispatched' via reopenBatchMember) before the task-status CAS runs, and never inspects the CAS's return value. If the CAS loses a race -- the task was already retried or moved to a terminal state by another concurrent request -- the function returns as if nothing happened, but the batch member has already been flipped open with no compensating rollback. The batch is left inconsistently reopened while the task itself never actually transitioned.

Correct: buildParkedResult keeps using parseResultRecord, which the sibling module documents as the tolerant reader for a result that may arrive as a JSON string. Both the object and string shapes are merged correctly, so chatId/subChatId/startMode survive a park.

buildParkedResult switches from parseResultRecord to an inline object-only check, but result-record.ts documents that a cloud-mirrored row's result can arrive as a JSON string. When rawResult is a string, the inline check treats it as falsy-typed and existing collapses to {}, silently dropping chatId/subChatId/startMode from the merged result. The park path is now out of sync with the reader contract parseResultRecord establishes.

Fixed: carryOnChat snapshots pendingChatRetry before clearing it, and the send is wrapped so a rejected sendMessage restores the previous marker instead of leaving the recovery state lost. The marker is only durably cleared once the wake message is accepted, matching retryChat's guard.

carryOnChat clears pendingChatRetry to null before sendMessage is even awaited, unlike retryChat right above it, which only clears the marker after the resend has gone out. If the socket drops or the send promise rejects, the clear has already happened and nothing puts the marker back -- the only recovery affordance for the parked message is gone, and the user has no way to retry it.

Correct: the read-check-append sequence now runs inside withFileLock, and the existing-ids read happens inside the critical section, so a concurrent call serializes and re-reads before deciding. The slow validation stays outside the lock, keeping the critical section short.

The uniqueness check reads the file, then a slow validation runs, then the append happens with no lock around the read-check-append sequence. Two concurrent registerEntry calls with the same id both see it absent and both append — the id-uniqueness invariant the file promises is broken exactly when intake is busy.

Correct: a floor shortfall is now surfaced as an error telling the caller to add qualifying rows, and no row's reserved flag is ever touched after intake — the once-assigned invariant holds for every row across its lifetime.

assignReserved documents that the reserved flag is decided exactly once at intake and that downstream consumers rely on it never changing. enforceReservedFloor silently mutates fresh rows' reserved flag to satisfy the floor, so a row that was assigned reserved:false can flip to true after consumers have already keyed on the intake value — the enforcement pass violates the module's own stated invariant instead of surfacing the shortfall.

Correct: the failure loop now selects only disposition:'blocking' events, so each writer owns a disjoint slice of the shared key space. A waived event produces exactly one record (kind:'waiver') and can no longer shadow or be shadowed by a failure record under the same key.

Both writer loops share keyOf as the record key, but the first loop emits EVERY event as a failure record without checking disposition. A waived event is first written as kind:'failure' and then re-written as kind:'waiver' under the same key — and a blocking event that shares runId/check with a later waived one is silently replaced. The failure loop must select only disposition:'blocking' events.

Correct: the shape-dependent field check now runs only when lint reported no problems, so a malformed entry gets its lint problem reported and the function returns normally — the never-throws contract holds for exactly the inputs lint rejects.

The exact entries lintEntry rejects (missing/malformed payload) are the ones that reach the next check anyway: checkEntry catches the lint error into problems but then unconditionally dereferences entry.payload.fields. For a malformed entry that path throws to the caller — breaking checkEntry's own never-throws, collect-all-problems contract precisely on the inputs it exists to report.
